# sources/test-tools/syzkaller/pkg/report/testdata/linux/report/378

Purpose: Linux reporter parse fixture for syzkaller. It encodes the expected parsed title `INFO: rcu detected stall in sys_inotify_init`, expected type `HANG`, alternate titles `INFO: rcu detected stall in __ia32_sys_inotify_init`; `stall in __ia32_sys_inotify_init`; `stall in sys_inotify_init`, corrupted flag `N`, and panic signal `N`. The raw body covers inotify syscall wrapper stall reporting; hang/watchdog classification; parser frame extractors must choose the blocked or stalled subsystem frame while avoiding scheduler, RCU, and watchdog helpers.

Important APIs, types, and functions: this file is static testdata consumed by `pkg/report/report_test.go`, not executable Go code. The relevant APIs are `parseReport`, `testParseImpl`, `Reporter.ContainsCrash`, `Reporter.Parse`, `Reporter.ParseFrom`, the Linux reporter implementation in `linux.go`, the generic `Report` fields in `report.go`, and crash type mapping via `pkg/report/crash.TitleToType`. Observed stack or title functions include `dump_stack`, `nmi_cpu_backtrace.cold`, `lapic_can_unplug_cpu.cold`, `nmi_trigger_cpumask_backtrace`, `arch_trigger_cpumask_backtrace`, `rcu_dump_cpu_stacks`, `find_next_bit`, `rcu_sched_clock_irq.cold`. Diagnostic tokens present in the complete fixture include `INFO:`, `rcu:`.

Control flow: `TestParse` enumerates `pkg/report/testdata/linux/report`, builds a Linux `Reporter`, reads this fixture, parses leading expectation headers until the blank line or `REPORT:` marker, then feeds the remaining console output to the reporter. For this file, the parser must return `INFO: rcu detected stall in sys_inotify_init`, preserve alternate titles `INFO: rcu detected stall in __ia32_sys_inotify_init`; `stall in __ia32_sys_inotify_init`; `stall in sys_inotify_init`, classify the report as `HANG`, and set corrupted/panicked behavior from the headers and log. The fixture has 67 total lines, including 62 pre-report/log lines and 0 explicit report lines; exact report-body comparison is `no`.

State and persistence behavior: the fixture persists expected parser state as text headers plus the raw kernel-console transcript. Runtime state is transient inside the tests: detected oops pattern, start/end offsets, report prefix length, title, alternate titles, crash type, panic/corruption flags, and any exact `Report.Report` bytes. No external state, network, filesystem mutation, or kernel interaction occurs when this file is used.

Dependencies and integration points: the file integrates with the syzkaller report package test harness and the Linux oops tables, stack parameters, title extractors, report-shortening logic, and dynamic title sanitizers in `linux.go` and `report.go`. At product level, the same parser path feeds syzkaller crash deduplication, dashboard grouping, guilty-file extraction, impact scoring, and maintainer routing; this fixture protects that path for inotify syscall wrapper stall reporting.

Risks and edge cases: regressions are likely if matching becomes too specific to one kernel version, timestamp format, architecture spelling, sanitizer wording, syscall wrapper name, or helper frame. The parser must avoid selecting generic helpers such as schedulers, softirq dispatch, RCU watchdogs, lockdep internals, KASAN report helpers, or USB/core wrapper frames when a more meaningful frame is available, while still preserving `INFO: rcu detected stall in sys_inotify_init` when the report is intentionally short or corrupted.

Test signals: a passing run requires `ContainsCrash` to agree with whether a title is expected, `Parse` to produce non-empty report bytes when a crash exists, parsed fields to equal the fixture headers, and `ParseFrom` to rediscover the same crash from its start offset while not returning the same crash after the end offset. This fixture specifically asserts `INFO: rcu detected stall in sys_inotify_init` with type `HANG` and exact report comparison `no`.
